exposure: myometrial glide flap technique for uterine dehiscence repair
cohort: The study included 38 pregnant women with 1-4 prior cesarean deliveries, desiring future fertility, who were diagnosed with uterine dehiscence and underwent cesarean section with a myometrial glide flap repair between March 2020 and March 2024.
finding: The myometrial glide flap technique effectively restored uterine wall thickness and integrity, enabling safe future pregnancies without recurrence of dehiscence or rupture in subsequent deliveries.
mod_finding: All subsequent deliveries following the repair occurred by cesarean section, with no cases of uterine dehiscence or rupture.
followup_time: Patients were followed prospectively for subsequent pregnancies, with the mean interval to the next pregnancy being 18.7 months and assessments at 6 weeks and 6 months postpartum.
gest_age: Subsequent deliveries occurred at a mean gestational age of 37.1 weeks.
